# soapysdr-module-fobos

**SoapySDR driver module for the RigExpert Fobos SDR**

- **Version recorded:** 1.1.0
- **Categories:** `sdr-hardware`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/rigexpert/SoapyFobosSDR>
- **Needs first:** `libfobos`, `libfobos-sdr-agile`
- **Install after:** `libfobos`, `libfobos-sdr-agile`

## What it does

A plugin for SoapySDR, the vendor-neutral SDR abstraction layer, that makes the RigExpert Fobos SDR usable through the generic SoapySDR interface, for a board running either firmware family.

## Why you would want it

It is what lets one program drive many different radios. SDR++, GQRX, CubicSDR, GNU Radio's Soapy source and a great deal else reach the Fobos through this module, so installing it is usually the difference between an application listing the radio and showing an empty device list. The module takes a `driver=fobos` argument and, per upstream's versions.txt, `index=` to choose between several boards.

## Before it will work

Both Fobos libraries (`libfobos` and `libfobos-sdr-agile`, which this unit depends on), the udev rule and group from the `fobos-sdr` hardware entry, and SoapySDR itself, which the build pulls in.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install soapysdr-module-fobos --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. ## How it installs

- git (cmake) — https://github.com/rigexpert/SoapyFobosSDR at `aa8d486cf03c5bc35fd7929e90e9a36c7f61ad8d`
  - build dependencies: `build-essential`, `cmake`, `pkg-config`, `libsoapysdr-dev`, `libusb-1.0-0-dev`
  - Built on 2026-10-02 in rootless containers the way this block runs it (cmake configure, `cmake --build --parallel 2`, `cmake --install` into /usr/local) after the two Fobos libraries were installed there: debian:13, ubuntu:24.04 and ubuntu:26.04 exit 0 in about 3 s with no warnings; kali-rolling (gcc 16) also exits 0 with four warnings. The module installs once, to /usr/local/lib/SoapySDR/modules0.8/ libFobosSDRSupport.so, and `SoapySDRUtil --info` then lists it (aa8d486) and `fobos` among the factories, with no ldconfig run. `--find="driver=fobos"` reports no devices, there being none. Built on x86_64 only; arm64 is unmeasured. Not measured: a board, streaming, or a client application.

Files its install rule leaves under the prefix, checked after the run and never copied or removed by the engine:

- `lib/SoapySDR/modules0.8/libFobosSDRSupport.so`

## Known problems

**Both libraries are needed to build it, whichever firmware the board runs.** A board on original firmware and one on the agile firmware show the same USB identifier and differ in bcdDevice only (see the libfobos unit); whether this module lists both kinds is upstream's code and not measured here. A module and its libraries must match or the radio is not listed rather than reported as broken: `SoapySDRUtil --info` shows what loaded and any dlopen error. The module is built into /usr/local/lib/SoapySDR/ modules0.8, which SoapySDR 0.8 searches. This is an untagged pin. **Not measured:** any board.
